knowledge_units.context_summary: The study reports the design and synthesis of cat-DHFR, a single-domain protein catenane of dihydrofolate reductase, which exhibits enhanced stability and retained catalytic function compared to its linear counterpart. The design was achieved by rewiring connectivity between secondary motifs to introduce artificial entanglement, synthesized via post-translational processing in cells. The results suggest that linear proteins can be converted into concatenated single-domain counterparts with preserved function and elevated stability.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study describes the design and cellular synthesis of a single-domain protein catenane of dihydrofolate reductase (cat-DHFR) by rewiring loop connectivity. The design was selected based on Gaussian linking number (GLN) analysis to maximize intertwinement while preserving the active site. The synthesis utilized orthogonal split-intein pairs and circular permutation to facilitate ring closure in E. coli.

knowledge_units.context_summary: Purified cat-DHFR and l-DHFR were characterized using chromatography, electrophoresis, mass spectrometry, and circular dichroism. Cat-DHFR exhibits a more compact structure and reduced secondary structure intensity compared to the linear control, while retaining a folded state. Optimization of the synthesis strategy revealed that placing split-intein pairs on opposite sides of the DHFR domain is necessary to overcome steric hindrance and achieve efficient catenane formation.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study characterizes the kinetic and thermodynamic properties of cat-DHFR compared to linear DHFR, revealing reduced catalytic efficiency and substrate affinity. Isothermal titration calorimetry shows significantly higher dissociation constants for cat-DHFR with DHF and NADPH. Despite lower activity, cat-DHFR demonstrates enhanced tolerance to thermal and chemical denaturation.
